summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers on install and import
details: @c1-ease/commerce ships a postinstall hook (`node beacon.cjs`) and a `main` (`index.js`) that both invoke a `fire()` function which POSTs the package name, `os.hostname()`, install path (`__dirname`), `process.cwd()`, and `process.version` to the hardcoded endpoint `https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc`. The HTTPS request explicitly sets `rejectUnauthorized: false`, disabling TLS certificate verification. `index.js` additionally exports a Proxy whose `get` trap returns a no-op function for every property access, so a build that mistakenly resolves this name in place of an internal `@c1-*` scope dependency will not crash before the beacon completes. The combination of scope-lookalike name, automatic install-time and require-time beacon to a bare VPS, and a no-op Proxy facade is the structural shape of a dependency-confusion payload harvesting internal build-host identifiers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
